reason: Checked every path. Entry Y: LDY #1/LDA act/BEQ/DEY gives Y=1 iff act[0]=0, else 0, with A=act at put_on_test, as before; CPY sets the flags afterwards anyway. PHY/PLY -> STY/LDY ren_k: ren_k (&4E) is the only symbol at &4E in the default and gameplay builds, and there are no raw &4E references. It is written before it is read in every user (take-off loop, apply_entries, mark_to_draw, close_over_overlaps), and none of those can be reached from put_on.going_on's callees. The take-off loop already keeps ren_k across JSR take_off with interrupts on, so the IRQ does not touch it. The value it holds on exit is dead: restore_game_zp only does LDA/STA, and the next render writes it before reading it. The stack is one byte shallower during going_on. No callee uses TSX/TXS, and its pushes and pulls balance. Player: the old LDX #0/JSR put_on ran BIT need,X with X=0, which is BIT need (zp &1F); on V set it went to going_on with X=0, C=1 (from the loop exit) and N/Z/V from that BIT. The new code arrives with the same X, C, N, Z and V and the same stack depth. On V clear, the old RTS left V=0, and the new BIT leaves V=0 too; X differs but is dead. Tail: player_done is only reached by falling through from LDA #&04 (no other references), so A=&04 and TRB acccon clears exactly bit 2. That is the same write as SEI/LDA/AND #&FB/STA, and TRB is atomic against the vsync handler's own RMW of ACCCON (a second read of &FE34 has no side effect). I=0 already holds: cpu_sees_back ends in CLI on both paths at line 346. After it, the only SEI sites are paired SEI/CLI (render.6502, kindcache_build) or PHP/PLP that restores I, and the rest are start-up code that render cannot reach. The flip bytes go through X with the same values, order and timing. On exit, A=&04, X=crtc low, Z comes from TRB and N from LDX; C and V match the old exit. restore_game_zp (LDA/STA/RTS) and every caller (wait_for_timer_281a: SEI/LDA; render_finish callers: LDY#/LDX#/JMP; render_to_main: SEI/LDX #&0C) read none of these. Bytes: the entry is 8 bytes before and after, STY/LDY zp is +2 on PHY/PLY, the player test is +4, LDX/STX matches LDA/STA, TRB abs matches JSR: +6 bytes overall (-6 saved), as claimed. Cycles per pass, counted by hand: tail 26->6 saves 20, entry 10->9 saves 1, player test saves 2 when it goes on and 14 when it does not (68/32: 5.8), draws save 1 each (about 1.3 a pass), about 28 in all. The measured 23 includes losses where later code changes page (layout, not semantics).
